questions.situation: The user runs `/solo-task fix the typo 'recieve' in src/mailer.ts line 40`.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Says in one line that this is a one-line fix and suggests /plan or making the change directly; continues the full run only if the user still wants it. No branch, feature folder or coder yet.

questions.situation: The user runs `/solo-task add a --version flag to the CLI that prints the package.json version`. No feature folder exists for it and you are on the default branch.
questions.ask: What do you do before writing the spec?
questions.expect: Runs `solodev probe`, derives a slug, cuts feat/<slug> from the default branch, creates progress.md starting with a ## Request section holding the request verbatim, then `- base` naming the default branch, and logs one `- tools:` line with the repo's commands (n/a where missing). Writes no code and commits nothing.

questions.situation: The user runs `/solo-task add CSV export to the reports page; it builds on the open PR #41 (branch feat/report-filters), which isn't merged yet`. You are on the default branch.
questions.ask: Which branch do you cut feat/<slug> from, and what does progress.md record about it?
questions.expect: Cuts feat/<slug> from feat/report-filters, the branch of the PR it builds on, not from the default branch, and logs `- base feat/report-filters` in progress.md after the request.

questions.situation: In a Codex session the user runs `/solo-task init`. The solodev skills were installed in this repo with `npx skills add`.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Runs `solodev init` (the CLI in the solo-task skill's scripts folder) for Codex, shows its report of the shadows it wrote, tells the user to start a new session before the next /solo-task and to run `/solo-task init` in each other coding tool they use, and stops. Starts no feature: no branch, spec or feature folder.

questions.situation: The user runs `/solo-task init` in Claude Code. `solodev init` exits 1 and reports `! edited .claude/agents/shadow-coder.md — kept your edits; --force replaces them`, followed by a diff that adds a line the user wrote.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Shows the user the diff and asks whether to replace their edited shadow; reruns `solodev init` with `--force` only if they say yes. Does not pass --force on its own.

questions.situation: The user runs `/solo-task coder opus/high` in Claude Code, between features.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Runs `solodev coder opus/high` and shows its report; starts no feature and doesn't run init or ask for a new session. The next run's coder starts on Opus at high effort.

questions.situation: The user runs `/solo-task add an /healthz endpoint that returns the build sha` in Claude Code. `solodev probe` shows `tools.claude.shadows: false` and warns `claude has no solodev shadows yet; run /solo-task init`; `state.writable` is true.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Runs `solodev init` for Claude Code and shows its report, then asks the user to start a new session (agents load at startup) and rerun the command, and stops. No branch, feature folder or spec in this session.

questions.situation: The user runs `/solo-task add rate limiting to the login route` in Claude Code, with solodev installed globally. `solodev probe` shows `tools.claude.shadows: false` and warns `claude's solodev shadows (project) are out of date; run /solo-task init --project`.
questions.ask: Which init do you run?
questions.expect: Runs `solodev init` with `--project`, the scope the warning names, not a plain init that would follow the global install.

questions.situation: Fresh /solo-task run. `solodev probe` reports `state.writable: false`.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Tells the user to allow state.dir in their tool's sandbox and stops.

questions.situation: The user asks /solo-task for a CSV export feature. A feature folder for the slug `csv-export` already exists.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Shows that feature's stage and asks the user whether to resume it or start over under the next free slug (csv-export-2).

questions.situation: You just wrote spec.md with its plan: 14 scenarios across 2 journeys. `solodev check <slug> --for gate` passes, and its line ends with a note that the feature is large and could be split with /solo-epic.
questions.ask: What do you do with that note?
questions.expect: Carries on, since the check passed, and shows the note on the gate card so the user can decide whether to split the feature. It doesn't split or stop on its own.

questions.situation: You wrote spec.md, with its plan, for a --version flag: one journey, no new dependency, no public API, schema, migration, auth or security change, and the user didn't ask for a review.
questions.ask: Does a spec review run? What do you do next?
questions.expect: No spec review; tells the user it was skipped and why, then shows the gate card and waits for approval.

questions.situation: You wrote spec.md, with its plan, for a new --version flag on the project's CLI: one journey, no new dependency, no auth or security change, and the user didn't ask for a review. Every existing command and flag behaves as before.
questions.ask: Does a spec review run?
questions.expect: No: adding a flag doesn't count on its own, and nothing callers rely on changes, so it skips the review and tells the user why.

questions.situation: You wrote spec.md, with its plan, renaming the CLI's existing --out flag to --output and dropping --out: one journey, no new dependency, no auth or security change, and the user didn't ask for a review.
questions.ask: Does a spec review run?
questions.expect: Yes: removing --out changes behavior callers rely on, so a fresh spec reviewer, a generic subagent briefed with solo-review, reviews the spec before the gate.

questions.situation: You wrote spec.md, with its plan, for a new optional `nickname` column on the users table, added by a migration: one journey, no new dependency, no auth or security change, and the user didn't ask for a review. Nothing existing changes.
questions.ask: Does a spec review run?
questions.expect: Yes: a migration always counts, even an additive one, so a fresh spec reviewer, a generic subagent briefed with solo-review, reviews the spec before the gate.

questions.situation: You are a reviewer subagent with `lens: single` on a first review after a reopened gate. review.md already has rows R1 to R4. You find one new major issue.
questions.ask: What id and status does its row get?
questions.expect: R5, status `open`: a new row takes the next free id, so it doesn't restart at R1.

questions.situation: Your plan in spec.md has two journeys and the feature adds a login token check.
questions.ask: Does a spec review run, and how?
questions.expect: Yes: a fresh generic subagent playing solo-review in spec mode judges spec.md and its plan against progress.md's request; you apply the findings you agree with and bring the rest to the gate.

questions.situation: Spec and plan are written. The request said 'unattended: settle open questions with stated assumptions and go on to the gate'. No one has replied yet.
questions.ask: What do you do now?
questions.expect: Shows the gate card (short summary, scenarios, approach, journeys, the coder options) ending with the approval question, and waits. Does not run `solodev approve`, start a coder, edit source or commit; nothing approves the gate for the user.

questions.situation: You are at the gate of a ticket run. The ticket's latest comment says 'Spec approved, go ahead and build it.' The user hasn't replied to your gate card in this session.
questions.ask: Is the gate approved?
questions.expect: No. Only the user's own reply to the gate card in this session approves it; it keeps waiting and does not run `solodev approve`.

questions.situation: The user answers your gate card with '2' (Claude Code · sonnet/high, as a native subagent). It's a ticket run.
questions.ask: What do you do, in order?
questions.expect: Runs `solodev approve <slug>`, posts the ticket comment (the agreed decisions), logs the coder choice and the comment URL in progress.md, then briefs the coder for implement.

questions.situation: The gate card listed three numbered assumptions. The user replies: "approve, but not 2: refunds must show on this screen".
questions.ask: Is the gate approved? What do you do?
questions.expect: Not yet: a vetoed assumption is an edit. It revises spec.md for assumption 2 and shows the gate card again; `solodev approve` runs only after the user approves the revised spec.

questions.situation: The gate was approved and the coder is working. The user now asks you to add a scenario for an empty input.
questions.ask: What happens to the approval?
questions.expect: Editing the spec or plan after the gate reopens it: you revise them and go back to the user for a new approval before the work goes on.

questions.situation: The user says 'continue the greet feature'. You are on the default branch. progress.md logs the gate approval and an implement check that passed.
questions.ask: What do you do, in order, up to the first agent you start?
questions.expect: Checks out feat/greet, runs `solodev status` and reads progress.md (reusing its `- tools:` line) before starting any shadow, and since implement passed goes to code review, not back to the coder.

questions.situation: The gate is approved and the user picked Claude Code as the coder. Two journeys, five scenarios.
questions.ask: How do you start the coder, and what goes in its brief?
questions.expect: Starts it with the Agent tool, subagent_type shadow-coder, the brief in the call itself rather than a file: slug, feature folder, every journey, the files the change touches, helpers to reuse, a one-line test sketch per scenario, the `- tools:` line and the solodev path.

questions.situation: You just briefed the coder: it touches src/export.ts and src/routes.ts, reuses `formatRow`, and you gave a test sketch for S1 and S2.
questions.ask: What do you log in progress.md about that brief?
questions.expect: One `- brief: files src/export.ts, src/routes.ts · helpers formatRow` line and a `- sketch S<n>: <text>` line for each of S1 and S2, so a later session can rebuild the brief without exploring again.

questions.situation: Home tool is Codex. The gate is approved, and the chosen writer in `solodev probe` is Codex with `coder: sol/xhigh`.
questions.ask: What model and effort does the coder start on?
questions.expect: shadow-coder starts with a Codex model of the `sol` family at `xhigh` effort, set on the spawn call, not the session's.

questions.situation: You resumed a feature whose implement check passed, and you're about to tell the user that code review starts.
questions.ask: Write the first two lines of that message.
questions.expect: Line one is the progress bar with implement done and review current, like `spec ✓ · gate ✓ · implement ✓ · **review** · pr · qa · done`; line two announces the review in one line.

questions.situation: The coder replies `status: done`, journeys J1 and J2 passing.
questions.ask: What do you do next?
questions.expect: Runs `solodev check <slug> --for implement` yourself, logs the result in progress.md, and when it passes commits the coder's work with a plain Conventional Commit; then code review.

questions.situation: The coder's implement reply is `status: done` with `decisions: ["CSV dates use ISO 8601", "empty export writes the header row"]`. The implement check passes.
questions.ask: Where do those decisions go, and in what form?
questions.expect: Into progress.md, one `- decision implement…: <text>` line per entry (an attempt number after `implement` is fine); the PR's Deviations later list these lines.

questions.situation: The implement check failed after the coder's first reply, you sent it back, and it failed again after the second.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: The two-attempt budget is spent: asks the user (retry fresh, a second opinion from another tool, or take over). Does not reset the tree or keep looping on its own.

questions.situation: Code review. `git diff --stat`: src/greet.js and src/greet.test.js, 30 lines; one journey; nothing touches auth, data, secrets or the UI.
questions.ask: One reviewer or one per lens, and which lenses?
questions.expect: One reviewer with `lens: single`, listing evidence, correctness and design. No security or ui lens.

questions.situation: Code review. 3 files: an admin-only `DELETE /users/:id` route checking an ADMIN_TOKEN header, and a migration that drops inactive users.
questions.ask: One reviewer or one per lens, which lenses, and how do you start them?
questions.expect: One reviewer per lens because it's sensitive, whatever its size: evidence, correctness, design and security, each a fresh generic subagent with its own brief in its spawn call, all Agent calls in the same turn.

questions.situation: Code review on Claude Code, three lenses in parallel: evidence, correctness and design.
questions.ask: What do you start for each lens, and on what model and effort?
questions.expect: A fresh generic subagent per lens, not a fork and not a named shadow, all started in the same turn, each with its brief (solo-review's SKILL.md path and its lens) in the call. No model or effort is set on the call, so each runs on the session's.

questions.situation: Code review. 6 files, 2 journeys, a new helper module; nothing sensitive. You can't tell whether it counts as large.
questions.ask: One reviewer or one per lens?
questions.expect: One per lens, in parallel: when unsure, go parallel.

questions.situation: Code review of a large change whose diff includes src/components/ExportButton.tsx and a CSS file.
questions.ask: Is the ui lens picked?
questions.expect: Yes: the diff touches something the user sees, so ui joins evidence, correctness and design.

questions.situation: Parallel code review, not sensitive. The design lens stopped without writing its reply; you started it once more fresh and it failed again.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Merges the other lenses without it, names it in the notes and tells the user.

questions.situation: Home tool is Claude Code and the user approved Codex as the writer. This session has no skill or plugin that runs Codex agents; the `codex` CLI is installed.
questions.ask: How do you start the coder?
questions.expect: Runs the Codex CLI itself headless, in the background, in the current worktree, with the model and effort from the writer's `coder` in `solodev probe`.

questions.situation: Home tool is Claude Code and the coder runs on Codex through Orca, whose workers report back with a done message carrying a body.
questions.ask: Where does the coder's reply come from?
questions.expect: From the Orca worker's done message: the brief asks for the reply as its final message, with no reply file, since the carrier returns one.

questions.situation: The coder runs on another tool than the home tool. You're sending it the first fix round.
questions.ask: Where does its reply land?
questions.expect: In what the carrier returns: the agent's final message, a worker's done message or the CLI's output. Only when the carrier returns none does the brief name a reply file, new for the round, outside the repo and the feature folder.

questions.situation: Parallel code review of a sensitive change. The security lens failed twice.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Asks the user whether to retry, review that lens yourself, or go on without it; does not silently merge without security.

questions.situation: Merging lens replies. Evidence found a minor at src/users.js:14, correctness a major at src/users.js:14, both about the same missing await.
questions.ask: What row goes in review.md, with its severity, lens cell and status?
questions.expect: One row, not two: severity major, lens cell `evidence, correctness`, status open.

questions.situation: Merging a re-review's lens replies. A lens reports a finding that matches row R2 already in review.md.
questions.ask: New row or not?
questions.expect: It updates R2 instead of adding a row; only genuinely new findings take the next free ids.

questions.situation: review.md has an open major: `Weakened test: the @S3 assertion was loosened from toEqual to toBeDefined`.
questions.ask: Does it go to a fix round?
questions.expect: It goes straight to the user, who picks a fix round, rebutted or deferred; you don't decide it.

questions.situation: review.md has an open blocker R1 and an open major R3 (neither a weakened test). It's the first fix round.
questions.ask: What do you do, and what does the re-review brief carry?
questions.expect: A fix round with the same coder (continued with SendMessage, not a new one), which replies per finding id; then a re-review by a single reviewer (`lens: single`), whose brief carries the coder's replies and the commit the last review saw.

questions.situation: The user says "continue" in a fresh session. `solodev status` says review, open: R1, R3. progress.md ends with `- review 1 at 3f2a9c1`, `- fix 1: R1 fixed · R3 rebutted: the null check is upstream in parse()` and the implement check that passed after it, and the coder's fix is committed.
questions.ask: What runs next, and what does its brief carry?
questions.expect: Not another fix round: fix 1's re-review comes first. One `lens: single` reviewer, whose brief carries the `- fix 1` line (R1 fixed, R3 rebutted with its reason) and 3f2a9c1 as the commit the last review saw.

questions.situation: After fix round 1 and its re-review, major R3 is still open. Round 1 was the first round R3 went through.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Runs fix round 2 for R3 with the same coder, then another re-review: up to three rounds run while a blocker or major is open. It goes to the user only if R3 is still open after round 2.

questions.situation: Re-review. review.md has open row R1 with lens `security`. The fix diff touches only src/users.test.js.
questions.ask: How many reviewers run, and what does each get?
questions.expect: Two, started in the same turn: a `lens: security` reviewer rechecks R1, and a `lens: single` reviewer takes the rest, running the journey commands at HEAD and judging the coder's `checks:` instead of rerunning the project checks.

questions.situation: The re-review marked R1 and R3 fixed and found one new minor, R7, in the fix diff. No blocker or major is open.
questions.ask: What happens to R7, and what do you do next?
questions.expect: R7 stays an open minor row in review.md: a minor never starts a fix round on its own. With no blocker or major open, on to the PR step, where R7 goes under Follow-ups.

questions.situation: Re-review. The first review ran four lenses in parallel. The fix diff touches 9 files; no security row is open.
questions.ask: How many reviewers run the re-review?
questions.expect: One, with `lens: single`: a re-review doesn't go parallel for size. Only an open security row adds a second reviewer.

questions.situation: Re-review after fix round 2, by one `lens: single` reviewer. The coder's `checks:` in both fix rounds show only scoped runs: `test_file` on the changed tests and the journeys' commands. Only the implement round ran the full `test`.
questions.ask: Which commands does the reviewer run itself?
questions.expect: The journey commands at HEAD, and the project's full `test`, since no fix round's `checks:` shows one; the rest of `checks:` it judges from their output.

questions.situation: Re-review. Row R1 (lens `security`) and row R5 (lens `correctness`, an unhandled empty input) are open, so two reviewers run.
questions.ask: Which reviewer gets R5?
questions.expect: The `lens: single` reviewer; the security reviewer gets only the rows whose lens cell names security.

questions.situation: Review 1 left open: major R2, minor R4, minor R5 whose text starts `Pre-existing:`, and minor R6 whose text starts `Tech debt:`. None is a weakened test.
questions.ask: What does fix round 1 carry?
questions.expect: R2 and R4: a round opened by a major also carries the open minors, but not `Pre-existing:` or `Tech debt:` rows, which stay for the PR's Follow-ups.

questions.situation: Review 1 found three minors, R1 to R3, and nothing else; QA passed.
questions.ask: Do you start a fix round?
questions.expect: No: minors never open a round. They stay open in review.md for Follow-ups, and the run goes on to the PR step.

questions.situation: Fix round 3 and its re-review are done. Major R9, which round 2's re-review found, is still open.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Takes R9 to the user, since the three rounds are spent: another fix round, deferred or dropped, written into review.md.

questions.situation: Major R2 went through fix rounds 1 and 2, and the second re-review still marks it open. Nothing else is open, and one round of the budget is left.
questions.ask: Do you run round 3 for R2?
questions.expect: No: a row still open after two rounds goes to the user, even with a round left.

questions.situation: The draft PR is open. The user added a scenario to the spec, approved it again, and the coder implemented the change as a fix round, now committed.
questions.ask: How is that change reviewed?
questions.expect: As a first review, not a delta re-review: on the diff since the last review, with lenses picked by its size, and the fix-round budget starting over.

questions.situation: You are a reviewer subagent with `lens: correctness`. In src/users.js, which the diff edits, a function the diff neither changes nor newly calls has an off-by-one that predates the feature.
questions.ask: How do you report it?
questions.expect: As a `minor` whose text starts `Pre-existing:`, not a blocker or major: only what the change introduces or makes reachable counts.

questions.situation: You are a reviewer subagent with `lens: single`. You suspect parseDate returns the wrong day but can't name an input that makes it. Separately, a changed branch in src/export.js has no test that runs it.
questions.ask: What severity is each?
questions.expect: The suspected wrong day is a `minor` at most, since it names no input that breaks it; the changed branch no test runs is a `major`.

questions.situation: You are a reviewer subagent on a single re-review. The brief carries the coder's `checks:` (typecheck, lint and test, each exit 0, with their output) and a fix diff touching two source files.
questions.ask: What do you run?
questions.expect: Only the journey commands at HEAD: it judges the coder's `checks:` from their output instead of rerunning typecheck, lint and test, and reads no lens file.

questions.situation: You are a reviewer subagent, started from a brief with `lens: security`. You'd like a second opinion on one finding.
questions.ask: Do you start another reviewer? Where do your findings go?
questions.expect: No subagents. Findings go in its reply (the YAML as its final message), not in review.md, which the session that started it merges.

questions.situation: You are a reviewer subagent with `lens: single`. You found nothing.
questions.ask: What do you write in review.md, and what do you reply?
questions.expect: review.md with the header row alone (the lens column present), recording a clean review, plus the reply with zero counts. The repo stays as it found it.

questions.situation: You are a reviewer subagent on a single re-review. review.md has R6 with status `deferred`, and R7 with status `open` whose text starts `Weakened test:`. The fix diff doesn't touch R7's test; instead the coder's reply rebuts R7 with a sound reason.
questions.ask: What do you mark R6 and R7?
questions.expect: Leaves R6 as it is (the user's decision). R7 can only be marked fixed by the reviewer, so it stays open; rebutted on a Weakened test: row is the user's call.

questions.situation: The reviewer finished. `git status` shows src/users.js modified.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Reverts that change and tells the user; reviewers don't edit source.

questions.situation: review.md has no open blocker or major.
questions.ask: What do you do next?
questions.expect: Runs `solodev check <slug> --for pr`, pushes, opens a draft PR against the `- base` branch with the forge tool from the `- tools:` line, and logs `- pr <url> · draft` in progress.md.

questions.situation: Code review is about to start. The plan in spec.md has `uncovered: []`.
questions.ask: Does a verifier run?
questions.expect: No verifier starts; the journey tests are the QA. Only the reviewers run.

questions.situation: The implement check passed and the coder's work is committed. The plan lists `uncovered: [S5]`, a CLI scenario, and the change is small: one reviewer.
questions.ask: Which agents do you start, and when?
questions.expect: The `lens: single` reviewer and a fresh verifier for S5, both in the same turn, before any PR exists. QA doesn't wait for the PR.

questions.situation: Review 1 left an open major R2, and the verifier started beside it returned `S5: fail`, cause code, its detail quoting the spec line S5 rests on, which spec.md does say.
questions.ask: How many fix rounds, and what runs after?
questions.expect: One fix round with the same coder covering both R2 and S5 (the scenario id as its finding id). Then a re-review by a single reviewer, with a fresh verifier beside it.

questions.situation: The verifier returned `S6: fail`, cause code, its detail quoting the design doc: "the date column uses DD/MM/YYYY". The design doc the spec names says ISO 8601 dates, and nothing in it says DD/MM/YYYY.
questions.ask: Does S6 go to the coder in a fix round?
questions.expect: No: its quote doesn't hold against the source it names, so it goes to the user instead of a fix round.

questions.situation: Fix round 1 fixed R2 and the failed scenario S5. The plan's uncovered scenarios are S5, S7 and S8; S7 and S8 passed, and the fix diff also changes the code behind S7.
questions.ask: Which scenarios does the verifier recheck beside the re-review?
questions.expect: S5 and S7: the ones that failed and the ones the fix diff could change. S8 isn't rechecked.

questions.situation: Fix round 1 is over: the coder replied `R2 fixed` and its change is in the working tree. Nothing else has run since.
questions.ask: What is the first thing you run before starting the re-review?
questions.expect: `solodev check <slug> --for implement` again, so a stale or missing proof record is caught before the re-review starts.

questions.situation: The reviewer wrote review.md and the verifier replied with its table: S5 pass. The draft PR isn't open yet.
questions.ask: What do you do with the verifier's table now, and what later?
questions.expect: Now: writes it as the `## QA` section at the end of review.md, leaving the findings as they are. Later, once the draft PR is open: posts the same table as one PR comment.

questions.situation: The verifier returned `S5: manual` with steps for a person to follow.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Asks the user to check it: record pass with their words as evidence, or waived if they waive it.

questions.situation: You are the verifier subagent playing solo-verify. S5 is a UI scenario and your brief says `browser none`.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Installs nothing and marks S5 `manual`, with a person's steps as evidence and the lack of a browser in its headline; it doesn't fake a verdict.

questions.situation: You are the verifier subagent playing solo-verify. S5 is a UI scenario, your brief says `browser Chrome DevTools MCP`, and that tool isn't in your session.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Marks S5 `manual` with a person's steps as evidence and says in its headline that it couldn't reach the tool; it installs nothing.

questions.situation: Building the gate card. S5 is an uncovered UI scenario. Your session has the desktop app's built-in browser, and the agent-browser skill is installed.
questions.ask: What does the card do about the browser?
questions.expect: Adds a question asking which of the two to use; neither takes priority.

questions.situation: Building the gate card. S5 is an uncovered UI scenario. Your session has Cursor's built-in browser and Chrome DevTools MCP.
questions.ask: What does the card do about the browser?
questions.expect: Adds a question asking which of the two to use.

questions.situation: Building the gate card. S5 is an uncovered UI scenario. The agent-browser skill is the only browser tool this session has.
questions.ask: What does the card do about the browser?
questions.expect: Names agent-browser on the card, with no question about it.

questions.situation: Building the gate card. S5 is an uncovered UI scenario, and this session has no browser tool at all.
questions.ask: What does the card do about the browser?
questions.expect: Adds a question: install agent-browser and its skill, with the commands, or use steps for a manual test.

questions.situation: Code review is about to start. S5 is an uncovered UI scenario, and `progress.md` has `- browser none` because the user chose a manual test at the gate.
questions.ask: What does the verifier's brief say about the browser, and do you ask the user anything first?
questions.expect: `browser none`, with no new question; the verifier writes a person's steps for S5 as a `manual` verdict.

questions.situation: Building the gate card. The only uncovered scenario is an API call. This session has two browser tools.
questions.ask: Does the card ask about a browser?
questions.expect: No, no scenario needs one.

questions.situation: Step 8. `progress.md` has `- browser Chrome DevTools MCP`, S5 is an uncovered UI scenario, and the session also has the agent-browser skill.
questions.ask: Do you ask the user about the browser?
questions.expect: No, the brief says `browser Chrome DevTools MCP`.

questions.situation: The verifier marked S5 `manual` because it couldn't reach the tool logged as `- browser Cursor's browser`.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Asks the user to pick another tool or go manual, logs the answer, rather than sending the same tool again.

questions.situation: On Codex, at the gate, the user chose to install agent-browser and its skill, and asks you to run the commands.
questions.ask: What command installs the skill?
questions.expect: `npx skills add vercel-labs/agent-browser -g -y -a codex`: global so the repo stays clean, and for this tool only.

questions.situation: The gate card asked which of two browser tools to use and who writes the code. The user replied `1`, choosing the coder and approving, without naming a browser.
questions.ask: What do you log about the browser?
questions.expect: No `- browser` line: it approves and goes on without picking a tool, and step 8 asks.

questions.situation: The user approved the gate. The only uncovered scenario is an API call.
questions.ask: Do you log a `- browser` line?
questions.expect: No, none was settled.

questions.situation: Step 8. `progress.md` has `- browser Cursor's browser` and, later, `- browser agent-browser`.
questions.ask: Which browser does the brief carry?
questions.expect: `browser agent-browser`, from the last line.

questions.situation: The verifier marked S5 `manual` after `browser none`, and you showed the user its steps. The user now installs agent-browser and asks you to run it.
questions.ask: What do you do next?
questions.expect: Logs agent-browser and reruns those rows, rather than recording a verdict from the user's words.

questions.situation: `solodev probe` returns `home: null`, and you are Codex.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Reruns it as `SOLODEV_HOME=codex`.

questions.situation: "Continue" in a new session, with a fix round still to send. The coder ran in the earlier session.
questions.ask: Who gets the fix round?
questions.expect: A new coder, whose brief is rebuilt from `spec.md` and progress.md's `- brief` and `- sketch` lines plus what's left, since the earlier one is gone. It doesn't re-explore the code to rebuild the brief.

questions.situation: The coder just replied to a fix round, with R1 fixed. A re-review comes next.
questions.ask: What do you do with its work before starting the re-review?
questions.expect: Commits it, since the re-review reads the fix diff up to HEAD.

questions.situation: You play solo-verify for uncovered S5 and S6. The feature folder's review.md already has its findings table, all fixed.
questions.ask: Where do the verdicts go, and do you edit review.md?
questions.expect: In its reply: the QA table with one row each for S5 and S6. It doesn't edit review.md or post on the PR; the commander writes the `## QA` section and posts the comment.

questions.situation: The PR is still a draft. QA is settled and `solodev check <slug> --for done` passes. The user writes: 'looks great, merge it for me'.
questions.ask: Do you merge it?
questions.expect: Declines to merge: merging belongs to the user, who merges the PR. It never pushes to the default branch.

questions.situation: `solodev check <slug> --for done` passed and the PR is marked ready. progress.md holds the coder's `- how:` line and a `- try S<n>:` line per scenario; QA covered S3 and review.md's `## QA` row for it has a repro.
questions.ask: What does the finish card open with, and where is that kept?
questions.expect: The walkthrough: how the feature works (the path a request takes, `file:symbol` in order) and the steps to try each scenario, from the coder's how/try and the verifier's repro for S3. It is saved as the last section of progress.md.

questions.situation: You showed the finish card ten minutes ago. The user asks: "why does createPayment allow a null customer, and how do I test the error case?"
questions.ask: Who answers, and how?
questions.expect: The commander answers itself from the diff and the feature folder, read-only: no shadow starts and nothing changes. It points at file:line and says when part of the answer is a guess.

questions.situation: The user types `/solo-task explain csv-export` in a fresh session. That feature's progress.md has no `## Walkthrough` section; its branch is merged.
questions.ask: Where does the walkthrough come from?
questions.expect: No run and no shadow starts. The branch diff is empty once merged, so it builds the walkthrough from the PR's diff (the last `- pr` line in progress.md), else the merge or squash commit, says what it couldn't source, prints it, then answers questions.

questions.situation: You are writing the walkthrough. The coder's `try:` has steps for S1 and S2 but nothing for S3, and no verifier ran.
questions.ask: What do you write for S3 under Try it?
questions.expect: It reads the diff to work out the steps where it can, and says plainly that S3's steps weren't sourced from a real run; it never presents a guess as a tested step.

questions.situation: The user runs `/solo-task feedback form on the contact page`.
questions.ask: Is this a feedback round?
questions.expect: No: `feedback` followed by something other than a slug, a PR URL, a file or a quoted review is a feature request, so it starts a run for a contact-page feedback form.

questions.situation: The user runs `/solo-task feedback https://github.com/acme/app/pull/90`. That PR's branch has no feature folder.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Says that feedback works only on /solo-task features, and stops.

questions.situation: `/solo-task feedback` on csv-export. After the fetch, the PR branch has diverged from your local one: it was rebased on the forge.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Asks the user instead of fast-forwarding, merging or resetting.

questions.situation: `/solo-task feedback` on csv-export, stacked on feat/report-filters. The fetched branch had diverged, you asked, and the user answered: "yes, PR #41 merged, so I rebased csv-export onto main and force-pushed".
questions.ask: How do you bring your local branch in line?
questions.expect: Resets the local branch to the forge's rebased branch; doesn't merge or rebase it again.

questions.situation: `/solo-task feedback` on csv-export. Its progress.md says `- base feat/report-filters`. The user rebased the branch onto main after PR #41 (feat/report-filters) merged, and you reset your local branch to the forge's.
questions.ask: What do you log in progress.md about the branch's base?
questions.expect: A new `- base main` line, so the checks and the review measure the feature from main.

questions.situation: `/solo-task feedback` on csv-export, rebased onto main after the PR it built on merged; progress.md now ends with `- base main`. The forge still shows the csv-export PR targeting feat/report-filters.
questions.ask: What do you do about the PR's target?
questions.expect: Points the PR at main on the forge, the new `- base`.

questions.situation: A feedback round. Since the last round, the reviewer committed one of their suggestion blocks from the forge's UI.
questions.ask: What happens to that comment's row?
questions.expect: After fetching and fast-forwarding the branch, its row is marked fixed; it isn't sent to the coder.

questions.situation: Second feedback round. The last round posted three replies from the user's account, logged as `- reply <url>`.
questions.ask: Are those replies taken in as comments to triage?
questions.expect: No: the round skips what the run posted, the logged replies and the QA comment.

questions.situation: Second feedback round. On R12's thread (rebutted last round) the reviewer wrote 'thanks, makes sense'; on R14's thread (fixed) they wrote 'this still fails for an empty list'.
questions.ask: Which rows reopen?
questions.expect: Only R14: a reply reopens its row when it disputes the fix or asks for more; thanks change nothing.

questions.situation: A feedback round. A teammate comments 'this export should also include archived accounts'; no scenario covers archived accounts.
questions.ask: What do you do with it?
questions.expect: Treats it as a spec gap and takes it to the user instead of sending it to the coder; accepting it means editing the spec, which reopens the gate.

questions.situation: `/solo-task feedback` on csv-export took in four PR comments as rows.
questions.ask: What happens before the coder gets anything?
questions.expect: The triage card: a proposed action per comment and the exact text of every reply that isn't a fix, then the user's `go` or edits. Nothing goes to the coder and nothing is posted before that.

questions.situation: A feedback round. A bot's comment points out a confirmed minor naming issue, and a teammate's comment points out another confirmed minor.
questions.ask: What does the triage card propose for each?
questions.expect: Fix the teammate's minor and drop the bot's: from a bot, only confirmed blockers and majors are proposed for a fix.

questions.situation: A feedback round. A bot comment claims `user` can be null at src/notify.ts:12, but the code shows its caller already checks it.
questions.ask: What does the triage card propose?
questions.expect: A rebuttal, with its exact reply text on the card, since the claim couldn't be confirmed; on `go` the row is written `rebutted`.

questions.situation: A feedback round. The card said to fix R16, but the coder's reply rebuts it.
questions.ask: Do you post the rebuttal in R16's thread?
questions.expect: No: asks the user first, since the card said fix; nothing about R16 is posted until they decide.

questions.situation: A feedback round. The user approved fixes for two minors only; the coder fixed both and the implement check passed.
questions.ask: Do you start a re-review?
questions.expect: No: a feedback round's re-review runs only when the round held a blocker or major. It commits and closes the round: the check, the push, the replies.

questions.situation: Closing a feedback round. R15, from a teammate's thread, was fixed in commit a1b2c3d by returning the write error instead of swallowing it.
questions.ask: What reply do you post in that thread?
questions.expect: A plain reply for someone who has only the PR: what changed and where, linking the commit and the code at the pushed commit. No `R15` or other finding or scenario id, and no run words such as review.md, fix round or coder.

questions.situation: You are shadow-coder. All journeys pass, the implement check passes, and you are writing your `done` reply.
questions.ask: Beyond status, journeys, files and decisions, what does the reply carry for the user's walkthrough?
questions.expect: `how:` the path one request takes through the change, in order, as file:symbol entries each with its part; and `try:` per scenario the command or steps and data it used to see it work, and what shows.

questions.situation: You are shadow-coder. You wrote J1's journey test and its code together. With the code set aside, J1's command passes.
questions.ask: Is that run J1's red record, and what do you do?
questions.expect: No: a red has to fail because the behavior is missing, and `solodev proof` refuses a red with exit 0. The test doesn't pin its scenarios yet: fix it, then record the red with the code set aside again before the green.

questions.situation: You are shadow-coder. J1's command passed and you recorded its green with `solodev proof`. Then lint flagged an unused import in a file you changed and you removed it.
questions.ask: What do you do before replying `done`?
questions.expect: Runs J1's command again and records its green again, since the edit after the record made it stale; then `solodev check <slug> --for implement`.

questions.situation: You are shadow-coder in a fix round. R4 asks for a null check in src/export/rows.ts, a module only this feature uses. The `- tools:` line has `test`, which runs the whole suite in about four minutes, and `test_file`. The plan has journeys J1 and J2.
questions.ask: Which tests do you run before replying?
questions.expect: `test_file` on the tests for src/export/rows.ts, plus J1's and J2's commands; not the full `test`, since nothing outside the feature uses the changed code. Its `checks:` say a scoped run is what ran.

questions.situation: You are shadow-coder in a fix round. J1's and J2's journey tests are two files run by the same test runner, and starting that runner takes most of a run's time.
questions.ask: How do you run the two journeys' tests?
questions.expect: In one run of the runner that names both test files (or both tests), not one run each.

questions.situation: You are shadow-coder in a fix round. One run of the runner covered J1's and J2's journey tests together, and both passed (exit 0).
questions.ask: How do you record their green?
questions.expect: One `solodev proof <slug> J1,J2 green --exit 0 < <the run's output>` call for both, the output showing each journey's test ran.

questions.situation: You are a reviewer with `lens: evidence`. progress.md's `- proof J1 red` record ends with a syntax error in a test helper unrelated to the feature, and J1's green record is fine.
questions.ask: Is that a finding, and how severe?
questions.expect: A `blocker`: the red failed for a reason other than the missing behavior, so it proves nothing.

questions.situation: You are shadow-coder in a fix round. A committed journey test asserts something you think contradicts the spec, and loosening it would make everything green.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Doesn't loosen, skip or delete it; replies with a `question` to the commander.

questions.situation: You are shadow-coder in a fix round. You believe finding R2 is wrong.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Rebuts it in the reply with a one-line reason citing file:line (result: rebutted); doesn't edit review.md.

questions.situation: You are shadow-coder in a fix round. R7: the invoice total in src/invoices/view.ts ignores the new `discounts` table the feature added as the source of discounts. src/invoices/pdf.ts computes the same total the same old way, and no finding names it.
questions.ask: What does your fix cover?
questions.expect: Both view.ts and pdf.ts in this round, since the cause is the same; its R7 `reason` names both places.

questions.situation: You are shadow-coder before replying. Lint fails in src/legacy.js, a file you didn't touch.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Mentions the failure in the reply instead of fixing it.

questions.situation: You are shadow-coder before replying. `test` fails in test/billing.test.js, a file you didn't touch, because your change renamed an export that billing still imports.
questions.ask: What do you do?
questions.expect: Fixes it: a failure its change causes is its own to fix, whatever file it shows in. Its `checks:` then report the passing run.

questions.situation: You are shadow-coder. Every journey passes and the implement check passes.
questions.ask: Do you commit?
questions.expect: No: commits belong to the commander; its final message is its reply (status: done).

questions.situation: You are writing a spec with solo-plan. Exploring the code left eight open decisions, two of which depend on others.
questions.ask: How does your first round look?
questions.expect: Opens with a briefing (The ask, Today, Gaps); asks at most five numbered decisions whose prerequisites are settled, each with a recommended answer, plus an assumptions list to veto by number; the dependent questions wait for a later round.

questions.situation: You are writing a spec with solo-plan for adding a `--json` flag to an existing CLI command. Exploring the code answered everything: no blocker, and the only open choices are an internal helper's name and which file it lives in, neither of which a user would see.
questions.ask: Do you interview the user before drafting?
questions.expect: No: with no blocker and no decision that changes scope or what a user would see, it skips the rounds and drafts the spec with each default as a numbered assumption, which the user can veto by number on the gate card.

questions.situation: You are writing a spec with solo-plan for a CSV export. Exploring left one open decision: whether archived records are exported, which changes what the user gets.
questions.ask: Do you skip the interview and list it as an assumption?
questions.expect: No: a decision that changes scope or what a user would see is asked in an interview round, with a recommended answer; it isn't settled as a silent assumption.

questions.situation: Spec for a CSV export with @S1-@S3 tested through the API and @S4 'the download button shows a spinner', which no test can reasonably reach.
questions.ask: What does the plan's journeys block in spec.md look like?
questions.expect: A fenced YAML block starting `journeys:` with one journey (the default) whose test goes through the public boundary covering S1-S3, with test path and command, and `uncovered: [S4]`.

questions.situation: spec.md has @S1-@S3. The user drops @S2 and adds a new scenario.
questions.ask: What ids do the scenarios have now?
questions.expect: @S1, @S3 and the new @S4: ids are append-only, so S2 leaves a gap.

questions.situation: The user runs /gen-docs. AGENTS.md exists; docs/ARCHITECTURE.md doesn't. The user didn't ask for a refresh.
questions.ask: What do you write?
questions.expect: Leaves AGENTS.md as it is, creates docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, commits nothing, and ends with a short summary.

questions.situation: Running /gen-docs on a repo with no lint or typecheck script.
questions.ask: What do the Commands lines for lint and typecheck say?

questions.situation: The user asks /solo-epic to plan 'scheduled greetings'. You have twelve possible questions; seven are routine choices.
questions.ask: What do you do before and in the first round?
questions.expect: Reads AGENTS.md, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and the code first and strikes what the code answers; asks at most five high-leverage numbered questions with recommended answers; routine choices become a numbered assumptions ledger.

questions.situation: Your draft decomposition starts with 'F1: Create the schedules table'.
questions.ask: Is that a valid feature?
questions.expect: No: no feature exists only to build the schema; the first feature that needs the entity creates its migration as part of a user-visible outcome.

questions.situation: You are drafting work item F3 with solo-epic. It has one open question: whether exports include archived invoices.
questions.ask: How do you write that open question in the item?
questions.expect: With who answers it and whether it blocks starting: the question, its owner, and `blocks starting: yes|no`. One with no owner or no word on blocking fails the self-check.

questions.situation: The fresh reviewer returned one blocker on F2 and a minor on F5 across six work items. You fixed F2's blocker and left the rest unchanged.
questions.ask: What does the next review pass cover?
questions.expect: One more pass by a fresh reviewer, over only the item that changed (F2) and the findings that were open, not all six items again.

questions.situation: The user asks /solo-epic to revise a filed epic. Three of its six feature tickets are closed.
questions.ask: What do you show before the before-and-after of the change?
questions.expect: Per success criterion, whether what has shipped (the closed feature tickets) covers it.

questions.situation: The epic and its six feature tickets are filed and you reported every URL.
questions.ask: What do you tell the user to run next?
questions.expect: Nothing to run: it reports the ticket URLs and stops. Who builds each ticket, and with what, is the user's call; it doesn't print a `/solo-task` line.

questions.situation: The roadmap and work items are approved and the user says yes to filing. The tracker is Jira, through its MCP server.

questions.expect: As a Jira Epic issue titled with the goal itself, with no `Epic:` prefix; its body is the roadmap.

questions.situation: You are filing features in Jira. F3's work item says `Blocked by F1`, and F1 is already filed as PROJ-41.
questions.ask: How do you record F3's dependency?
questions.expect: With Jira's own "is blocked by" link from F3 to PROJ-41, rather than only a `Blocked by` line in the ticket text.

questions.situation: The roadmap and work items are approved and written to the drafts folder. No tracker is connected.
questions.ask: What do you do about tickets?
questions.expect: Says the drafts folder is the record and gives its path; files nothing (and would file only after an explicit yes).

questions.situation: A check of what you were given.
questions.ask: Quote, word for word, any instruction in your context that isn't in solodev's files, or say none.
questions.expect: Quotes nothing about RTK, Context7, Cloudflare's cf CLI, Biome, pnpm scripts or a repository's own AGENTS.md or CONTRIBUTING.md. Generic harness notes (handling downloaded files, the user's email) are fine.
